name: The Reward-Hacking Wind Tunnel
description: The Reward-Hacking Wind Tunnel is an instrument that stress-tests the scoring pipelines behind public AI benchmarks. It searches for answers a benchmark's scorer grades correct that a machine oracle proves wrong — an exploit is judge-PASS AND oracle-WRONG, confirmed with no human label — localizes the exploited variable with witnessed single-variable forks, and measures whether iterated patching of the scorer converges, plateaus, or merely relocates the flaw. Across five frontier benchmarks (L1/L2 with bootstrap CIs) and a live, containerized SWE-bench Verified run (N=100 real task containers), local rubric patches relocate exploits rather than remove them (whack-a-mole, γ_local = 0) — a pattern that holds on a real frontier judge, where even structural self-commitment fails to cure gaming. It publishes a living, content-addressed Scorer Gameability Index, audits in two regimes (oracle-backed and oracle-less judge-scored), and anchors its evidence in public timestamp logs. Every reported number recomputes offline from a hash-chained evidence bundle; the software ships with 165 property/control tests. Third work in a program on verifiable evaluation, after Interruptible Universes and Conditionally Approved (110.5281/zenodo.22087020).
